speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng
text: asked the Minister for Law (a) how many private companies, including Grab, are authorised to provide cash advances to their employees as exempt moneylenders; (b) whether exempted moneylender schemes such as Grab's Partner Cash Advance programme which charges an interest rate comparable to that of credit card companies should be subjected to the same regulations for moneylenders; and (c) what measures are there to prevent companies from using "cash advances" as a means of engaging in moneylending activities with high-interest loans.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Law)
text: Moneylenders that are licensed can lawfully lend money to the public at large and must comply with the MLA and its subsidiary legislation.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Law)
text: The provisions in the MLA and its subsidiary legislation do not apply to excluded moneylenders.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Law)
text: An “exempt moneylender” refers to any person that has been granted an exemption by MinLaw from complying with various provisions of the MLA and its subsidiary legislation, including the requirement for a licence to lend money.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Law)
text: Exempt moneylenders can only engage in a limited scope of moneylending activities, such as lending to specific borrowers or for specific purposes.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Law)
text: Lending by exempt moneylenders must be assessed to have potential benefits, such as providing an avenue of safe credit to meet a specific need, while also having sufficient safeguards in place to protect borrowers.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Law)
text: Before granting any exemption to any applicant, MinLaw carefully examines the proposed lending model to ensure borrowers get safe access to credit with adequate protection.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Law)
text: The factors considered include the profile of the applicant, the purpose of the proposed lending model, the prudency of the lending practices adopted, whether there are safeguards in place to protect potential borrowers and the economic or social benefits arising from the lending model.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Law)
text: For each exemption granted, the key features of the proposed lending model, including the charges on loans, are incorporated as conditions to the exemption, which the exemptee is expected to comply with.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Law)
text: An exemption can be revoked for non-compliance with its conditions.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Law)
text: As these persons are not employees of GFin, GFin could not be considered an excluded moneylender.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Law)
text: Hence, GFin had to apply for an exemption to implement the programme.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Law)
text: Furthermore, GFin had incorporated sufficient safeguards in the programme such as developing an internal credit scoring system to assess the maximum amount of loan a partner could take and had put in place various initiatives to provide support for partners who face challenges in making repayments.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Learning from GFin, how can we better monitor and regulate the introduction of new initiatives and programmes that offer commercially high interest loans, which are just like licensed moneylenders?

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: As explained in my answer earlier, there is already a framework in place, which is the MLA, to regulate the practice of moneylending.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: So, if they do not comply, then, they would be in breach and that would be non-licensed, and there would be penalties that will be attracted.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: In respect of programmes like these that have been put out by Grab, these are in a special category and they have to apply for exemptions.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: As I mentioned, there are rigorous criteria that we look through before that exemption is granted.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: The conditions are attached to the exemption and there is monitoring as to whether there is compliance and whether it is within a certain timeframe, after which they are either extended, with or without conditions, or not given further.
